People's Majlis

Committee Minutes of the People's Majlis

21st meeting of the Information and Communication Technology Committee

21 October 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis, G (Committee Room 7)

Start time: 10:30

{Presiding: Chair of the Committee; Member for Milandhoo constituency, Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir}

Speech by the Chair:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Assalaamu alaikum. Welcome to the Information and Communication Technology Committee of the People's Majlis. We are sitting today for the 21st meeting. Today, too, we are continuing the work of reviewing the Digital Identity Bill. At this point I will first read out the committee's attendance. Honourable Member for Maduvvari constituency, Ahmed Zahir; Honourable Member for Alifushi constituency, Abdul Latheef Abdul Rahman; Honourable Member for Kulhudhuffushi South constituency, Farhath Mohamed; Honourable Member for Makunudhoo constituency, Adam Shafeeq. These are the members who have joined the committee at this time. So, at this point I will proceed with the work of reviewing the bill. Thank you.

Speech from the secretariat desk:
Yes! From Article 63. Chapter 8, Security Measures. Security, integrity and confidentiality. Article 63. (a)- In connection with this Act, the Digital Service, identity information providers, service providers, and data processors working on behalf of those parties shall take technical and administrative arrangements and measures in accordance with the Cyber Security Act and relevant international standards and principles, to ensure the security, accuracy and confidentiality of the identity information under their care, and the extent to which that information is available. (b)- The measures to be taken under (a) of this Article shall include at least the following. (1)- Taking protective measures to prevent the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, misuse or alteration of identity information. (2)- Taking protective measures to prevent access to identity information by an unauthorised party or the disclosure of that information to an unauthorised party. (3)- Establishing procedures for taking action in relation to a security incident, and reporting principles; and (4)- Conducting penetration testing in the security audits to be carried out regularly

. (c)- In determining the measures to be taken under (a) of this Article, regard shall be had to the following. (1)- The quantity of identity information and its importance. (2)- The likelihood of harm being caused to, or danger arising for, a registered person as a result of the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, misuse, alteration, or unauthorised disclosure of identity information. (3)- The extent to which identity information has been processed or is expected to be processed. (4)- The cost of taking specific measures or of establishing a specific technology, system or facility, and the resources available for doing those things. (d)- For the purposes of (c)(4) of this Article, a decision to take or not to take a particular measure under this Article, having regard to the cost of taking specific measures or establishing a specific technology, system or facility and the resources available for doing those things, shall be made in a manner that does not fall below the minimum standard of security protection that must be established to achieve the objectives of this Act. (e)- The mandatory measures, the optional measures that may be taken, and the conditions and procedures for taking those measures, for implementing the matters set out in this Article, shall be determined in the regulation made under this Act. Responsibility of the Cyber Security Agency. Article 64. The National Cyber Security Agency shall ensure that the Digital Service is acting in accordance with the Cyber Security Act in operating the digital identity system of the Maldives. Chapter Nine. Other matters relating to operation of the system. Conducting audits of the system. Article 65. (a)- In order to ensure that it is acting in accordance with the objectives, security and protection, and principles of confidentiality of personal information set out in this Act and the regulation made under this Act, the Maldives Digital Service shall regularly audit and review, to the extent necessary and in a reasonable manner, the programmes of the digital identity system of the Maldives and the procedures established for running those programmes, as well as the programmes of service providers and the procedures established for running those programmes, in the manner set out in the regulation made under this Act. (b)- The audits stated in (a) of this Article shall be conducted having regard to the risks in the system, in a manner that ensures reasonable protection for information relating to any security

or privacy-related vulnerability that may exist in the system, in accordance with all relevant laws and regulations. Monitoring compliance of service providers. Article 66. (a)- The Digital Service shall establish a system to monitor and assess the extent to which service providers participating in the digital identity system comply with this Act, the regulations made under this Act, the instructions issued by the Digital Service under this Act, and the guidelines and standards it publishes. (b)- The monitoring system stated in (a) of this Article shall be formulated in a manner that includes principles for determining the extent to which service providers adhere to this Act and the standards made under this Act, reporting on those matters, and procedures for holding those parties accountable in cases of non-conformity with the established standards. (c)- In order to monitor and assess the extent to which service providers participating in the digital identity system comply with this Act, the regulations made under this Act, the instructions issued by the Digital Service under this Act, and the guidelines and standards it publishes, it is mandatory to submit the reports required to be submitted to the Digital Service under this Act and the regulation made under this Act, and to provide the information requested by the Digital Service as soon as possible. Taking action. Article 67. (a)- If a service provider, a data processor, or a party licensed to issue verifiable credentials contravenes this Act or a regulation made under this Act, the Digital Service shall have the discretion, depending on the gravity of the matter, to take one or more of the following measures. (1)- Imposing a fine; or (2)- Imposing a fine together with an administrative measure or measures. (b)- If a party stated in (a) of this Article contravenes this Act or a regulation made under this Act, that party may be fined as follows. (1)- For the first time, a fine of an amount not exceeding five hundred thousand rufiyaa; and (2)- For each time beyond the first, a fine of an amount between five hundred thousand rufiyaa and one million rufiyaa. (c)- In addition to imposing a fine under (b) of this Article, the Digital Service shall also have the discretion to take the following measures against a party stated in (a) of this Article. (1)- Temporarily suspending or revoking the licence issued to that party to participate in the system; or (2)- Temporarily suspending or revoking the licence issued to a party licensed to issue verifiable

credentials; or (3)- Giving written guidance to the service provider, data processor, or party issuing verifiable credentials, or ordering it to do specific things to rectify the contravention within a specified period. (4)- Taking another measure set out in this Act. (d)- If a party stated in (a) of this Article fails to rectify the contraventions within the period specified in an order issued by the Digital Service under (c)(3) of this Article, the Digital Service shall have the discretion to impose a fine of an amount not exceeding one thousand rufiyaa for each day that passes without the matter being rectified. (e)- A fine determined under this Article shall be a fine graded in a proportionate manner, having regard to the gravity of the contravention committed by a party stated in (a) of this Article and the adverse impact that contravention would cause. (f)- The procedure to be followed by the Digital Service in determining fines under this Article, and the matters to be considered in determining fines, shall be set out in the regulation made under this Act. And the matters to be considered in so determining fines shall include at least the following. (1)- The nature of the contravention committed by the licensed party, the circumstances in which the contravention occurred, and the extent of that party's responsibility for it. (2)- The seriousness of the contravening act and the impact it caused. (3)- The extent of attention and cooperation given by the licensed party in bringing the contravention to the attention of the Digital Service and in rectifying the contravention. (4)- Whether that party obstructed bringing the contravention to the attention of the Digital Service or any work done in connection with it, or whether or not that party responded to what the Digital Service requested. (5)- The good faith of a licensed party in fulfilling the responsibilities set out in accordance with this Act and the regulations made under this Act, or the extent of evidence that the party deliberately misled in any of those matters. (6)- Whether or not the Digital Service had to take a temporary or urgent measure because of the contravening act. (7)- Whether the licensed party has repeated the contravention, and if repeated, the number of repetitions and over what period they were repeated, and for how long the contravention continued. (8)- Any measure previously taken or fine previously imposed

against the licensed party, if any. (g)- In order to ensure compliance with this Act, the Digital Service shall have the discretion to order service providers, data processors, and parties issuing verifiable credentials to provide reasonable information relating to the activities they carry out under this Act. (h)- No measure under this Article shall be taken against a party suspected of contravening this Act or a regulation made under this Act except after giving that party notice of it and an opportunity to respond. (i)- The notice given under (h) of this Article shall include the following information. (1)- The date on which the suspected contravention occurred or is believed to have occurred, and the nature of the contravention. (2)- Details of the suspected contravention or prohibited act; and (3)- The matters considered in assessing the suspected contravention and in determining the amount of the fine intended to be imposed in connection with it, and if any measure under (c) of this Article is intended to be taken, that fact. (j)- If dissatisfied with a decision made by the Digital Service under this Article, the party to whom the decision applies shall have the right to submit that decision to court within three months from the date the decision is made. Filing and investigating complaints. 68 (a)- If it is believed that the Digital Service or a service provider has acted contrary to the obligations and protection principles set out in this Act, an eligible person or a registered person shall have the opportunity to file a complaint in relation to it. And a resolution that produces a result for such complaints shall be provided within a reasonable time. (b)- In filing a complaint under (a) of this Article, the eligible person or registered person shall file the complaint within thirty days from the date on which it becomes known that an act contrary to this Act has occurred. (c)- The Digital Service shall respond to a complaint filed under this Article within thirty days from the date the complaint is filed. (d)- If the parties to whom a decision made by the Digital Service under (c) of this Article applies are dissatisfied with that decision, that party shall have the opportunity to submit the matter to court within three months from the date the decision is made. (e)- The Digital Service shall establish simple and easy procedures for filing complaints and resolving those matters, in the manner set out in the regulation made under this Act. Charging fees. Article 69. (a)-

In order to fulfil the responsibilities and duties set out in this Act and the regulation made under this Act, the Digital Service shall have the discretion to charge fees for the activities carried out by the Digital Service, in the manner determined in the regulation made by the Ministry under this Act. (b)- A regulation made for the purposes of (a) of this Article shall include at least the following. (1)- Determining the amount of the fee or the manner in which the fee to be charged will be calculated. (2)- Determining the time and manner in which the fee must be paid. (3)- Determining the fines that may be imposed if the fee is not paid as determined; and (4)- The circumstances in which a determined fee or fine may be refunded. (c)- Notwithstanding (a) of this Article, no fee shall be charged under the regulation made under this Act for the following activities. (1)- For registering in the digital identity system; or (2)- For issuing a digital identity number or a token or authenticator linked to it. (d)- Fees and fines collected under this Act shall be deposited into the Consolidated Revenue Fund of the State in the manner set out in the Public Finance Act. Circumstances exempting from liability. Article 70. (a)- The Digital Service shall not be liable for any loss suffered by a service provider, a third party or any other party as a result of any of the following matters. (1)- A technical problem encountered by the system; or (2)- Human error; or (3)- Fraudulent authentication of a registered person's information. (b)- For the purposes of (a)(3) of this Article, even if a registered person's information is fraudulently authenticated, the Digital Service shall not bear any liability for the resulting loss only if it is not the result of bad faith, intent, or negligence. (c)- If a registered person's information has been fraudulently authenticated in bad faith, intentionally, or due to negligence of the Service, any party wishing to seek compensation for the resulting loss shall have the right to file a case in court in accordance with the relevant law. Annual report. Article 71. The Maldives Digital Service shall prepare and publicly publish an annual report on the operation of the digital identity system. And that report shall include at least the following information. (a)- Statistics showing, including information on sex, age, disability status, and region of registration,

the number of people registered in the system from among eligible persons. (b)- Details of assessments made to identify difficulties in registering in and using the system and to resolve those matters. (c)- Information relating to service providers active in the system. (d)- Details of how the system is being used, in light of technical standards. (e)- A summary of the results of independent audits conducted in relation to the security of the system, ease of access to services, and the protection provided to personal information stored in the system, and the measures taken or intended to be taken by the Digital Service in connection with those audits; and (f)- A summary of the costs incurred in operating the system and the fees charged under this Act. Chapter Ten. Transitional matters. Continuation of conflicting agreements when the Act comes into force. Article 72. (a)- Agreements made with the Digital Service or any other relevant State body by service providers and data processors entrusted with the responsibility of implementing the system established for authenticating the digital identity of the Maldives before this Act comes into force shall continue to the extent that they do not conflict with this Act, the regulations made under this Act, and the principles, procedures and standards issued by the Digital Service under the authority of this Act. (b)- Notwithstanding (a) of this Article, even if any provision of an agreement made with service providers or data processors for the purposes of the digital identity system established before this Act comes into force conflicts with this Act, a regulation made under this Act, or the principles, procedures and standards issued by the Digital Service under the authority of this Act, upon this Act coming into force it shall be mandatory for the parties to those agreements to comply with this Act, the regulations made under this Act, and the principles, procedures and standards issued by the Digital Service under the authority of this Act. And the parties to those agreements shall make the amendments required to those agreements within 6 months of this Act coming into force, in order to bring those agreements into line with this Act. (c)- If parties that participated in the digital identity system established before this Act comes into force do not wish to participate in the system established under this Act, and wish to bring that party's participation to an end, within 3 months from the date this Act comes into force that

party shall submit a request to the Digital Service to bring its participation to an end. Migration plan. Article 73. (a)- The digital identity system established before this Act comes into force, and that system's database, shall be fully migrated to the digital identity system established under Article 19 of this Act and that system's database within 24 months from the date this Act comes into force. (b)- The system established before this Act comes into force and that system's database shall continue until they are migrated to the digital identity system established under this Act in the manner set out in (a) of this Article. (c)- In order to migrate the system in operation before this Act to the digital identity system set out in this Act in the manner set out in (a) of this Article, the Digital Service shall formulate a migration plan and implement the following. (1)- Ensuring that, for migration from the system in operation before this Act to the digital identity system and that system's database required to be established under Article 19 of this Act, the migration is to a database designed in accordance with the conditions and standards set out in this Act and the regulations made under this Act, and, to facilitate that, entering into information-sharing agreements with identity information providers, and doing everything necessary to make the changes and upgrades required to the system in operation before this Act or to further improve that system. (2)- After migrating to the digital identity system established under this Act in the manner set out in (a) of this Article, conducting an independent audit and preparing and publishing a report on the integrity of that system, its operational standard and the accuracy of the information. Reforming the system for issuing identity numbers. Article 74. (a)- The sequential numbering system used on identity cards of Maldivian citizens, work permits and visas at the time this Act comes into force shall be changed to a unique identity numbering system as set out in Article 36(c) of this Act within the period set out in Article 73 of this Act. (b)- In order to change from the sequential numbering system to a unique identity numbering system as set out in Article 36(d) of this Act, within 6 months from the date this Act comes into force, the identity information providers, in conjunction with the Digital

Service, shall formulate and implement a plan on how the following will be done. (1)- The changes required to the currently established system in order to generate unique identity numbers in accordance with the principles and conditions set out in relation to digital identity numbers in this Act and the regulations made under this Act, and if a new system needs to be established, how that will be done. (2)- The order in which new unique numbers will be issued in place of the sequential numbers currently issued to citizens, residents and other foreign parties, the procedures those parties must complete to change their numbers, the periods within which those things must be completed, and how those things will be done. Chapter Eleven. General provisions. Making regulations. Article 75. (a)- Unless otherwise stated in this Act, all regulations required to be made under this Act shall be made and administered by the Digital Service. (b)- The Digital Service may issue the principles, guidelines, instructions and circulars required to implement and administer this Act. (c)- The regulations required to be made under this Act shall be formulated and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives within 6 months of this Act coming into force. Commencement of the Act. Article 76. This Act shall come into force on the date on which 12 months are completed from the date this Act is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives. Definitions. Article 77. Unless the way a word or expression is used in this Act specifically conveys another meaning, the following words and expressions shall have the meanings given to them below. (a)- "Minister" means the minister of the government ministry entrusted at the time with the responsibility of implementing policies relating to establishing and operating the national digital identity system. (b)- "Ministry" means the government ministry entrusted at the time with the responsibility of implementing policies relating to establishing and operating the national digital identity system. (c)- "Digital identity system of the Maldives" means the system established under Article 19 of this Act. (d)- "Eligible person" means a person who fulfils any of the conditions set out in Article 27(a) of this Act. (e)- "Person" or "party" includes natural persons and legal persons. (f)- "Natural

person" means a reference to a human being, including Maldivians and foreigners, as compared to a legal person. (g)- "Application" means a software programme designed to perform specific tasks or provide specific services. (h)- "Application programming interface" means the rules and protocols that determine how different software systems and applications can interact and exchange information. (i)- "Interoperability" or "interoperable" means the ability of different technology systems, devices and software applications to interact without barriers in an interconnected manner, exchange information and work together in a reasonable way. (j)- "Data breach" means unauthorised or accidental access to, alteration of, damage to, disclosure of, use of, or destruction of personal information due to a lapse in the security of that information. (k)- "Foundational identity database" means the electronic databases established in the Maldives, and the systems connected to them, set out in Article 19(b)(1) of this Act. (l)- "Database of the digital identity system" means the database of the digital identity system of the Maldives set out in Article 28 of this Act. (m)- "State institution" includes all institutions and offices operating under the executive power, all institutions and offices operating under the legislative power, all independent commissions established under the Constitution and law, the offices of independent posts, all institutions and offices operating under those bodies, and all institutions, offices and places operating under the judicial power. (n)- "Department of National Registration" means the government office entrusted with the system for managing matters relating to civil registration, including registering information on children born and persons who die in the Maldives. (o)- "Person lacking the capacity to make decisions of their own volition" means any person who, due to a mental or physical condition, does not have the ability to make independent decisions in their own affairs or to understand the consequences that may result from such a decision, and who has to depend on another person to look after that person's legal responsibilities and interests.

(p)- "Law enforcement agency" means any State institution charged under a law with the responsibility of preventing criminal offences and investigating such offences. (q)- "Legal guardian" means any person who, by a judgment of a relevant court, carries out the legal responsibilities of a minor or of a person who does not have the capacity to make decisions of their own volition. (r)- "Representative" means a parent, legal guardian or family member who represents an eligible person or a registered person on behalf of that eligible person or registered person in accordance with the law. (s)- "Resident" means foreign parties living in the Maldives having obtained a residence visa to stay in the Maldives under a relevant law. (t)- "Maldivian identity card registration system" means the electronic database of Maldivian identity cards established and maintained by the Department of National Registration under Law No. 23/2022 (Act on Registration of Births and Deaths and Issuance of Birth Certificates and Maldivian Identity Cards), the systems connected to notification and registration, and changes made to that database in the future. (u)- "Visa registration system" means the electronic database storing the identity information of persons issued visas, established and maintained by the relevant State institution entrusted at the time with the responsibility of managing matters relating to visas other than work permits or work visas, which is established and maintained by a relevant State institution, the systems connected to notification and registration, and changes made to that database in the future. (v)- "Work permit registration system" means the electronic database storing the identity information of persons issued work permits, established and maintained by the relevant State institution entrusted at the time with the responsibility of managing matters relating to work permits of residents, the systems connected to notification and registration, and changes made to that database in the future. (w)- "Caching" means storing data in frequently accessed temporary storage

areas in order to speed up future requests (future requests) in digital systems. (x)- "Personal information" has the meaning given to that expression in the Personal Data Protection Act. (y)- "Personal Data Protection Act" means the law in force at the time in the Maldives relating to the protection of personal information. (z)- "Maldives Digital Service" or "Digital Service" means the Maldives Digital Service set out in the Maldives 2.0 Digital Transformation Act. (aa)- "National Cyber Security Agency" means the National Cyber Security Agency set out in the Cyber Security Act. (ab)- "Cyber Security Act" means the law in force at the time in the Maldives to ensure the protection of the cyber environment of the Maldives. (ac)- "Privacy Commissioner" means the Privacy Commissioner set out in the Personal Data Protection Act. (ad)- "Data processor" means any party that processes personal information on behalf of the Digital Service, identity information providers and service providers. This meaning includes State institutions and legal persons. (ae)- "Attributes" means characteristics relating to a person.

Speech by the Chair:
Yes! With the second reading of the review of the Digital Identity Bill concluding at this point today, I intend to close today's committee at this point. Thank you.
